source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Adding one irrelevant sentence to grade-school math problems (GSM-IC) badly hurts every prompting method. Few problems are solved across all distractor types.
numbers: Of base problems solved with greedy decoding, no more than 18% are solved consistently across all distractor types. Macro accuracy under distractors is under 30% for most settings (e.g. code-davinci-002 COT macro 6.0, LTM 18.0 with plain exemplars). Models: code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003.
limits: Old models (2023). Distractor is a single sentence; effect is largest when it overlaps in role or entities with the question. Newer models are more robust but see GSM-NoOp.
agent_relevance: Extraneous text in the prompt is a measurable cost. Drop task-irrelevant text before the model reasons.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Mitigations tested: an instruction to ignore irrelevant text, exemplars that contain distractors, and self-consistency. All help somewhat; none removes the problem.
numbers: Instruction 'feel free to ignore irrelevant information' lifted COT micro accuracy 72.4 to 77.8 and LTM 77.5 to 80.6 (code-davinci-002); macro COT 6.0 to 15.0. Exemplars with distractors raised COT micro to 76.8 and LTM to 80.7. Self-consistency with 20 samples: correct answer present in 99.7% of problems.
limits: Instruction gains are modest in the macro metric. The S2A paper later found the same instruction gave no consistent gain on LLaMA-2-70B-chat.
agent_relevance: An ignore-this instruction is a weak fix. Removing the text (code-side filter) is the stronger lever; sampling then voting recovers answers but only if the selector is independent.

source: Weston and Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention (is something you might need too)
finding: Have the model rewrite the context to keep only relevant, unopinionated parts, then answer from the rewrite. This is a direct 'drop irrelevant text' method inside a prompt pipeline.
numbers: Factual QA with opinions in the prompt: LLaMA-2-70B-chat 62.8% to 80.3% with S2A (oracle prompt 82.0%). GSM-IC with in-topic irrelevant sentences: 51.7% to 61.3%; accuracy up about 12 points for random distractors and 10 points for in-topic ones. Instructed prompting ('ignore irrelevant') gave no consistent gain. A prompt-only variant reached 74.5% vs S2A 80.3%.
limits: One model family (LLaMA-2-70B-chat), 200 factual prompts judged by GPT-4. Costs an extra generation. The rewriting step is itself model-judged, so it can drop needed facts.
agent_relevance: Strong candidate for a pre-step: a separate call that extracts only what the question needs, then solve from the extract. Compare against code-side filtering where possible.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Accuracy is highest when the needed passage is at the start or end of the context and lowest in the middle, a U-shape. Longer context windows do not fix it.
numbers: Multi-document QA: GPT-3.5-Turbo accuracy can fall by more than 20 points; with 20 and 30 documents the worst case is below its closed-book score of 56.1%. Extended-context variants match their short-context versions (GPT-3.5-Turbo 16K 56.0 vs 56.1 closed-book). Key-value retrieval: query placed before and after the data gives perfect accuracy at 300 pairs for GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K); without it the worst case is 45.6%.
limits: Models of 2023 (Claude-1.3, GPT-3.5, MPT, LongChat). Newer long-context models improved on retrieval but not on use, per later work.
agent_relevance: Put the question both before and after the data, and put key evidence at the edges. More retrieved text can be worse than none.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Lost in the Middle (architecture comparison)
finding: Architecture matters: encoder-decoder models are robust when sequences are shorter than their training length; decoder-only models cannot attend from context to a query placed after it.
numbers: Flan-UL2 and Flan-T5-XXL show little position sensitivity within training length, and the U-shape returns on longer inputs. Query-aware contextualisation (query before and after) fixes key-value retrieval but only slightly helps multi-document QA.
limits: Mechanism is partly the causal mask, partly position bias. Not all tasks gain.
agent_relevance: Repeat the task statement after long material. Integration order matters because earlier tokens cannot see later ones.

source: Ok and Lee (2026) Lost in the Prompt Order: Revealing the Limitations of Causal Attention in Language Models
finding: Search summary only: in multiple-choice QA, context first then question and options (CQO) beats question and options first then context (QOC) by more than 14 points across many models and datasets. Authors blame the causal mask, which stops option tokens seeing the context.
numbers: Over 14 percentage points CQO over QOC, as reported in a search snippet; the full table was not read.
limits: Not opened (fetch blocked). Treat as unverified until the PDF is read.
agent_relevance: Order is an integration factor: place the material the options depend on before them. Verify before relying on the figure.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with Large Language Models
finding: Reordering premises without changing the task hurts reasoning. Models do best when premises appear in the order the proof uses them, so the reader need not jump back and forth.
numbers: Deductive reasoning: permuting premise order drops accuracy by over 30%. GPT-4-turbo and PaLM 2-L fall up to 20 to 30 points; Gemini 1.0 Pro and GPT-3.5-turbo fall from over 65% to below 25% (over 40 points). R-GSM benchmark: 220 pairs of original and reordered GSM8K problems, all models lower on the reordered set.
limits: Logic puzzles with distracting rules plus a math reorder set; 2024 models. Effect grows with the number of rules.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM analogue to physical integration: lay out information in the order it will be used, so steps need not search across the prompt.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: GSM-NoOp adds a seemingly relevant but inert clause to a math problem. Models often turn it into a wrong operation.
numbers: Drops of up to 65% across all state-of-the-art models; Phi-3-mini over 65% drop; o1-preview also drops significantly. Using more shots, even of the same question, did not close the gap.
limits: Authors read this as pattern matching, not a load effect. The clause is plausible, so it differs from random filler.
agent_relevance: Plausible but irrelevant statements are the worst extraneous text. Strip them rather than tell the model to ignore them.

source: Levy, Jacoby, Goldberg (2024) Same Task, More Tokens: the Impact of Input Length on the Reasoning Performance of Large Language Models
finding: Padding a fixed task with irrelevant text lowers reasoning accuracy well below the maximum context. Chain of thought does not fix it.
numbers: Average accuracy across tested models falls from 0.92 to 0.68 at 3,000 tokens of padding. Padding similar to the task usually hurts more than dissimilar text. CoT helps GPT-4, Mixtral 8x7B, Mistral Medium and GPT-3.5 at short length but does not stop the decline; for Gemini Pro it worsens with length. Next-word perplexity correlates negatively with reasoning accuracy. 600 samples per plotted point.
limits: Task is two-fact QA with controlled padding; 2024 models.
agent_relevance: Length itself taxes reasoning. Keep prompts short even when facts are retrievable.

source: Du et al. (2025) Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval
finding: Even when models retrieve all needed evidence with 100% exact match, accuracy still falls as input grows. This holds with whitespace padding and even when distractor tokens are masked out of attention.
numbers: Drops of 13.9% to 85% as input length rises, within the claimed context limit, across 5 open and closed LLMs on math, QA and code. With irrelevant tokens masked, drops of at least 7.9% remain; HumanEval Llama3 drops 50% under masking vs 19.4% with space.
limits: Not a clean extraneous-load test: masked tokens still shift positions. Authors say length itself matters.
agent_relevance: Two causes to separate: distractor content and sheer length. Both argue for a short, curated working context.

source: Du et al. (2025) Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval (retrieve-then-solve fix)
finding: Fix: have the model first recite the relevant evidence, then answer from the recitation alone in a fresh short prompt.
numbers: Mistral-v0.3-7B on GSM8K with essay distractors at 0, 3750, 7500, 15000, 26250 tokens: baseline 70.6, 49.3, 43.4, 41.6, 35.5; with the fix 76.2, 71.4, 66.7, 69.1, 66.7 (up to 31.2 points). GPT-4o on RULER QA1 88.2-90.4% baseline, 92.2% at 4K; QA2 gain up to 4 points.
limits: Gains largest for weaker models; GPT-4o gain is small. Recitation can drop facts.
agent_relevance: Matches an integrate-then-solve step: extract, then reason in a clean short context.

source: Jiang et al. (2024) LongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression
finding: Question-aware compression plus reordering of retrieved documents raises accuracy while cutting tokens. Removing noise helps, not just cost.
numbers: NaturalQuestions (20 documents), GPT-3.5-Turbo: up to +21.4% with about 4x fewer tokens; 94.0% cost reduction on LooGLE. Ablations: removing any component (question awareness, dynamic ratio, subsequence recovery) lowers accuracy.
limits: Gains are largest when the answer document sits mid-context. Compressor is a small LM; the 'up to' figure comes from one benchmark.
agent_relevance: Evidence that cutting tokens by relevance to the question beats keeping everything. Compression must be question-aware, not generic.

source: Cuconasu et al. (2024) The Power of Noise: Redefining Retrieval for RAG Systems
finding: Related-but-wrong retrieved passages hurt most; random unrelated passages can help. So extraneous text is not uniformly harmful.
numbers: One distracting document cuts accuracy by up to 0.24 (-25%); with several, accuracy falls by more than 0.38 (-67%) in some cases. Adding random documents raised accuracy by up to 35% (Llama2, 4 retrieved docs, +0.07 on NQ-open).
limits: The random-noise gain is a boundary condition; mechanism untested and not a design recommendation.
agent_relevance: Near-miss content is the dangerous kind. Do not assume more context is neutral; test the noise type.

source: Niu et al. (2025) Llama See, Llama Do: A Mechanistic Perspective on Contextual Entrainment and Distraction in LLMs
finding: Models give higher probability to any token that appeared earlier in the prompt, even random tokens. Distraction is partly mechanical and tied to specific attention heads.
numbers: Counterfactual prompts show stronger entrainment than factual ones. Removing the identified entrainment heads reduces the effect significantly on the country-capital relation test set (logit delta and token ranks shift). Authors report 3-10% overlap with induction-type heads.
limits: Measures logits on controlled completions, not task accuracy under production prompts.
agent_relevance: Mere presence of a token raises its chance of being used. Text you do not want echoed or used should not be in the prompt.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Attention Entropy is a Key Factor: An Analysis of Parallel Context Encoding with Full-attention-based Pre-trained Language Models
finding: Splitting context into separately encoded pieces (a machine version of separated sources) degrades performance; unusually high attention entropy is the key factor. Attention sinks and selective mechanisms reduce the loss.
numbers: Naive parallel encoding degrades results; two fixes (attention sinks, selective mechanism) reduce entropy and recover part of the gap. Table figures not extracted here.
limits: Architecture-level, not a prompt-level test. Related work suggests splitting can help unless cross-chunk synergy is high.
agent_relevance: Supports the idea that mutually dependent pieces should be encoded together, not separately.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in Large Language Models: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning (ICE benchmark)
finding: Adding task-irrelevant context (context saturation) lowers multi-hop exact-match accuracy in capable models. Length alone does not explain it.
numbers: Gemini-2.0-Flash-001: control 0.85, 0.82 at 20% load, 0.78 at 50%, 0.72 at 80% saturation; slope -0.003 per % load (p<0.001). Long Control 0.82 vs control 0.85 (p=0.45). GPT-4o-0613: 0.65 to 0.55, trend not significant (p=0.07), about 32% of outputs lacked final answers. Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B and Mistral-7B scored 0% everywhere. 200 questions, 10 replications each.
limits: Independent-author preprint with heavy caveats. Three of five models at floor, GPT-4o confounded by truncation. Attentional residue effect not significant (p=0.12).
agent_relevance: Extraneous text effect is real but modest in strong models: about 13 points at 80% clutter. Gains appear only where the model can already do the task.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in Large Language Models (hop recall)
finding: Intermediate-hop recall drops under clutter even more than final accuracy, so loss is in carrying facts, not only the answer.
numbers: Gemini hop recall 0.90 control to 0.75 at 80% saturation; GPT-4o 0.80 to 0.65. Residue-condition drop correlates with task similarity (Gemini r=0.42, p<0.01; GPT-4o r=0.35, p<0.05).
limits: Similarity measured by embedding cosine; small design.
agent_relevance: Distractor tasks similar to the real task do the most harm. Keep unlike material out of the working prompt.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad: A Synthetic Natural Language Reasoning Benchmark With Tunable Length, Intrinsic Difficulty, and Distractor Density
finding: A benchmark built on cognitive load theory varies intrinsic difficulty, distractor-to-signal ratio (extraneous) and length separately. Length is the dominant stressor; distractor ratio gives U-shaped effects.
numbers: 22 reasoning LLMs; 100 puzzles per cell for open models (14,000 per model), 10 per cell for Gemini-2.5, gpt-5 and DeepSeek-R1. Steepest decline between N=20 and N=50 (DS-Llama-70B 0.89 to 0.66; Qwen3-8B 0.71 to 0.40). At N=250 only gpt-5 (0.76) and o3 (0.68) exceed 50%. Strong models are near-flat to distractors (o3, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash); others are worst at intermediate ratios and recover at extremes (gpt-5-mini 0.84 to 0.86, gemini-2.5-flash-lite 0.38 to 0.53).
limits: Synthetic logic puzzles; mapping distractor ratio to extraneous load is the authors' choice. Max 32K context.
agent_relevance: Extraneous load is not monotone in LLMs: a mix of signal and noise hurts most. Length matters more than distractor share.

source: Wang et al. (2026) Beyond Accuracy: A Cognitive Load Framework for Mapping the Capability Boundaries of Tool-use Agents (ToolLoad-Bench)
finding: Tool-use accuracy falls as extraneous load (ambiguous queries, distractor tools) rises, for every model tested, much like the effect of intrinsic load.
numbers: Accuracy decays exponentially with total load; fitted load sensitivity k: xLAM2-32B 0.034, GPT-4o 0.067, Claude 3.7 0.073, Qwen3-32B 0.075, Qwen3-8B 0.085, Gemini2.5-pro 0.088. Llama3.3-70B reached about 23% accuracy; xLAM2-32B stayed above 60% at high extraneous load. Authors: confusing presentation is 'as significant a hurdle as inherent task complexity'. 200 base instances from BFCL.
limits: Extraneous load is a hand-designed score; a fine-tuned tool model beat larger general models.
agent_relevance: For agents with tools: fewer distractor tools and clearer queries each count as load reduction. Expose only needed tools per step.

source: Shang et al. (2026) United Minds or Isolated Agents? Exploring Coordination of LLMs under Cognitive Load Theory (CoThinker)
finding: A multi-agent system designed with CLT (split intrinsic load among agents, compress shared state to cut transactional load) helps on reasoning-heavy tasks and adds overhead on easy ones.
numbers: Pilot: attention entropy 4.44, 4.80, 5.04 at task complexity levels 1 to 3. Hard-task perplexity falls with richer instructions (120.50, 88.97, 85.35) but easy-task perplexity does not (3.37 to 3.45). Paired Holm tests: 16 of 25 comparisons significant on LiveBench; one category shows +16.2% vs IO, +15.5% vs CoT, +18.3% vs SR. Debate-style baselines degrade as rounds accumulate.
limits: Gemini models mostly; attention entropy and perplexity are proxies for load, not measured load. Gains vanish on instruction-following tasks.
agent_relevance: Compressing shared state between agent steps is the multi-agent version of integrating sources. Add structure only for high-load steps.

source: Search result: no direct LLM test of the classic split-attention contrast (searches run 2026-10-28)
finding: Several searches found no study that tests the classic contrast (integrated vs separated sources) in text-only LLMs under the split-attention name. Closest are the position, order, distractor, length and multi-turn studies in this file.
numbers: 0 direct studies found in web, arXiv and OpenAlex searches this session.
limits: Negative result from searches only; studies in unindexed venues could exist.
agent_relevance: The effect is plausible by mechanism (causal mask, attention entropy, multi-turn shards) but unproven as a named effect. Our own prompt-format ablation would be new evidence.

source: VMMU authors (2025) VMMU: A Vietnamese Multitask Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark
finding: Separating question text and options from the image evidence (instead of one rendered page) improves multimodal models. Separation helps because text embedded in an image interferes.
numbers: 2,548 questions, 7 tasks. Original to separated: open-source VLMs 41.32 to 50.97 (+9.65); non-thinking closed models 57.83 to 66.40 (+8.56); thinking closed models 80.16 to 82.26 (+2.10); overall mean 52.89 to 60.86 (+7.97). Models include Gemma-3-27B, Qwen-2.5-VL-72B, Llama-4 Scout and Maverick, Mistral-Small-3.2, Mistral-Medium-3, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Sonnet-4.0, GPT-4.1, o3, Gemini-3-Pro.
limits: Direction is opposite to human split attention (separation helps) because the cost is text-in-image decoding, not mental integration. Only a model subset was run; page read through a summarising fetch.
agent_relevance: Do not assume integrate always wins. Where one channel needs decoding (text in image, dense tables), give it as clean text beside the evidence.

source: Kang et al. (2026) ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
finding: An agent loop that compresses observations and history into short notes, with compression rules tuned from failure analysis, uses fewer tokens and often scores higher. Irrelevant information is named as a cause of degradation.
numbers: Reduces peak tokens by 26-54% on AppWorld, OfficeBench and multi-objective QA while keeping or raising task success; improvements of up to 46% reported for smaller models (abstract wording).
limits: Abstract and introduction read; per-benchmark tables not extracted. Compressor is an LLM, so it may lose details.
agent_relevance: A working agent-loop use of this subfield: keep a lean state, prune old observations, tune the pruning rule from failures.

source: Lindenbauer et al. (2025) The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
finding: In a software agent, replacing old tool outputs with a placeholder (observation masking) halves cost and matches or slightly beats LLM summarisation on solve rate.
numbers: SWE-agent on SWE-bench Verified, five model configurations. Qwen3-Coder 480B: masking is 52% cheaper than the raw agent and improves solve rate by 2.6 (units as printed in the text). A hybrid cuts cost a further 7% vs masking and 11% vs LLM summary.
limits: One benchmark and scaffold; limited evidence for OpenHands. Masking can break tasks that need old outputs.
agent_relevance: Cheap code-side pruning of stale tool output is enough. Fits the 'code selects' guardrails: no model call needed to drop text.

source: Laban et al. (2025) LLMs Get Lost in Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: When one instruction is spread across turns (sharded) instead of given whole, performance drops sharply. Information spread over time acts like separated sources.
numbers: 15 LLMs, 200,000+ simulated conversations, six tasks: average drop 39% (about 90% single-turn to 65% sharded). Drop appears even in two-turn conversations. Split into a minor aptitude loss and a large reliability loss. Concatenating all shards in one turn (CONCAT) removes underspecification; recap and repetition help only in part: SNOWBALL (repeat info each turn) mitigates 15-20% of the deterioration on GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini.
limits: Simulated users and sharded instructions; real chats may differ. RECAP needs knowing the last turn.
agent_relevance: Strongest LLM evidence for the integration effect: give the full task in one consolidated block and re-consolidate state before answering.

source: Sclar et al. (2024) Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design
finding: Meaning-preserving format changes (separators, casing, field order) change accuracy hugely, so layout is never neutral.
numbers: Accuracy varies by up to 76 points for LLaMA-2-13B between equivalent formats; sensitivity persists with larger models, more shots and instruction tuning.
limits: Mostly few-shot classification with older models; format differences are not integration differences as such.
agent_relevance: Any layout ablation must test several formats or the result may be a format quirk. Report the spread.

source: Fu et al. (2025) Exclusion of Thought: Mitigating Cognitive Load in Large Language Models for Enhanced Reasoning in Multiple-Choice Tasks
finding: Search summary only: having the model rule out wrong options first reduces load and improves multiple-choice performance.
numbers: No figures read.
limits: Not opened; claim comes from a search result and the authors' own CLT framing.
agent_relevance: Possible operator for option-heavy tasks. Read before use.

source: Cognitive Overload Attack (arXiv 2410.11272)
finding: Search summary only: prompts built to overload the model with extra tasks and clutter can jailbreak safety-trained models.
numbers: Attack success up to 99.99% across several models, per search snippet.
limits: Not opened; adversarial setup, not a prompt-design study.
agent_relevance: Clutter can switch off safeguards, so a lean prompt is also a safety measure.
